title: Contact pressure and normal force skewed at nodes where a contact surface turns a corner
body:
A secondary node's unit normal is the sum of the area vectors of all its secondary faces. Where a general-contact surface turns a corner, those faces point in different directions, for example:
- an end face meeting a z = const face of a one-layer plane-strain hex model;
- an outer face meeting an end face.

The reported nodal `pressure` (−f·n over the support) and the contact's `normal_force` are then projections onto a tilted normal. The forces themselves are unaffected, and so are the displacements.

## Reproduce
1. Run `c_ring(true, 0.15)` in `crates/solver/tests/contact.rs`: a 3D one-layer hybrid C-ring closing on itself.
2. Run the same ring in plane strain (`planar_c_ring`).
3. The displacements agree node for node to 1e-5, and so does the contact force vector (−3.29e-5 in both).
4. `normal_force` differs: 0.00595 in 3D against 0.00816 in 2D. The nodal pressures at the closed nodes are about 25 % lower in 3D (0.044 against 0.058).

## Expected
Take each node's normal and normal force from the faces that carry the contact at that node, e.g. weighted by each face pair's support ∫Φ_A. Faces with no overlap at the node should not tilt the normal. The 3D and plane-strain rings should then report the same normal force and pressures.
